summary: The busiest week on this account since mid-August — 15 messages against 10 in the previous fourteen days — and the first week in over a month in which ALTR actually delivered something. Mica sent a full 11-link reel-inspo drop on Sep 15, closing a commitment that had been overdue since Aug 13 (a 33-day gap) and ending the run in which every single ALTR message was a request. Stephski reinstated the pre-invoice heads-up she dropped on Sep 1 ('your invoice will be sent tomorrow... it would be great if you could initiate a OF withdrawl today', Sep 14), apologised unprompted for the banking back-and-forth, and wished the client a good trip. Derrek broke 46 days of silence on Sep 16 to answer a question within two hours and twenty minutes. And the client came back: after a fortnight in which she opened nothing and wrote under 30 words, Callie asked her first substantive question in weeks, made a decision, and paid inside two days ('Thank you, have sent:)', Sep 17). That is the good news, and it is real. The bad news is that all of it happened on top of a money position that got measurably worse. Last week's file named one thing that should be blocked outright: 'Does the Sep 1-14 invoice (due ~Sep 15) go out on top of three unconfirmed cycles? If it does, that is the fifth stacked request and should be blocked, not just flagged.' It went out on Sep 15, on schedule, with the same 'to avoid any pausing in work' condition — and not one of the three open cycles was mentioned. The Aug 15-31 invoice, which carried a 7-day deadline that expired on Sep 8, has now gone 17 days without a single word from anybody on either side; it is not late so much as lost. The Aug 17 wire is 32 days unverified and the Jul 15-31 duplicate question is 41 days unanswered. ALTR has now issued five invoices and confirmed receipt of exactly two — the last confirmation was on Jul 23. Stephski also reversed the one fix that demonstrably worked: 'Noting I have changed the currency back to USD, as when you send in pounds we are losing a bit of money each time, its accounted for a few hundred dollars at this point' (Sep 15). GBP invoicing was the accommodation that turned a 6-day payment cycle into a 2-day one, and it was promised to this client in writing on Jul 7 by Alex Camus ('We will make sure the exchange is on the next invoice'). It has been withdrawn, the FX burden moved onto the client, and she absorbed it without argument: 'yes I will just send the amount in USD and pay the fee to make it easier'. In the same breath she raised the closest thing to a complaint she has ever made — 'Is the account info going to change each time? Just because I have to change the entire payee and to do that I have to actually speak to my bank to verify' — the third change to ALTR's banking details in 70 days. Derrek's answer to that is the most consequential sentence in the window: 'no its just the name of it was abbreviated before and for some people it went through but for others it didn't'. That is ALTR confirming that its own account name caused client wires to fail for some payers — said sixteen days after the Aug 17 wire, sent against exactly those abbreviated details, was last asked about. Nobody connected the two. And Derrek's reappearance cuts the other way too: he was in this chat on Sep 16, read a message, and replied about a bank account — while the Instagram suspension he owns sat at 87 days and the client's own Aug 31 statement that her main account is still gone sat 18 days unanswered. For six weeks the finding was that the owner was absent. This week he was present and chose something else. Vivek is 51 days in the chat with zero messages. Michelle is 32 days silent with 48 client videos and 72 days of unfulfilled post links behind her. Mayson opened a third ask — 'do you have a facebook account available to use?' — without booking the call Callie accepted on Sep 6 (11 days) or explaining crystalmila.vip (26 days), and closed the thread with 'Okay'. Three membership changes happened in eight days (adds on Sep 10 and Sep 17, a removal 50 seconds after the invoice posted on Sep 15) and not one introduction was posted.

health.rationale: Up 2 from 42 — the first non-negative movement since Aug 8 (82 → 74 → 66 → 54 → 50 → 42 → 44) and a deliberately small one, because the uptick is behavioural and the deterioration is financial. Three things genuinely improved and they are the three that matter for retention. ALTR delivered a real deliverable for the first time in 33 days (Mica's 11-link inspo drop, Sep 15, closing the account's longest-running content commitment). The client re-engaged: she opened a thread, asked a substantive question, made a decision, thanked two people and paid within two days — after a fortnight of near-total withdrawal in which she initiated nothing. And the owner reappeared, answering her inside 2h20m after 46 days of silence. Volume rose from 10 messages in fourteen days to 15 in seven. On any leading indicator of churn, this week was better. The score does not rise further because the single largest risk on the account got worse in three distinct ways. (1) The fifth invoice went out on Sep 15 on top of three unconfirmed cycles, carrying the same pause-work condition, with none of the three acknowledged — the exact action last week's file said should be blocked rather than flagged. (2) The Aug 15-31 invoice has now passed 10 days beyond its own stated deadline and 17 days since issue without one word from either side; it has effectively fallen out of the relationship. ALTR has issued five invoices and last confirmed a receipt on Jul 23. (3) The GBP accommodation — the only change that ever measurably improved this client's payment behaviour, and one promised to her in writing on Jul 7 — was withdrawn and the exchange-rate burden moved onto her, justified by an ALTR-side loss of 'a few hundred dollars' that was raised while two of her own wires sit unacknowledged. Separately, the largest issue on the account hardened rather than aged: the IG suspension is 87 days old, her Aug 31 statement that her main account is still gone is 18 days unanswered, and Derrek was demonstrably present in the chat on Sep 16 without touching it. That is a different and worse finding than absence.
